The Bangkok config sets no transfer penalty, passenger mode mapping, intermodal access and egress, range query, transit route selector, chained departure or capacity feedback. Every condition that selected the old fallback was absent, so this bundle was already on the round-based engine before issue 116. Removing the fallback is therefore a no-op for this scenario.

output_experienced_plans.xml differs, but solely in the order of child elements inside attributes, for example routingMode before aborted versus aborted before routingMode. InternalAttributes wraps a std HashMap<String, Value> with default RandomState, so serialization order varies per process. Plan content is unchanged; byte-for-byte plan comparison is not currently reproducible.
762896 legs, 127533 persons and 173375 aborted legs, all identical to the pre-issue-116 run. The multi-partition abandoned-leg defect is untouched by issue 116 and remains a separate open defect.

Issue 116 delivers the coverage and consolidation goal, not a speedup for default configurations. The roughly 9x per-person routing gap against Java on this bundle is therefore still unexplained by the fallback and needs separate profiling of prepare_plan to attribute to transit search, car routing or per-trip overhead.
